clue.text: Had home team to wear a plain colour?

indicators.note: whoever wears a garment sits inside it, so the team goes within the colour

blocks.note: red is a plain colour, the outer piece
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A football club debating whether its home strip should be a single plain shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had home team' reads as a club playing at its own ground; 'Had home' is the definition and the team goes inside the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to live there, so the past tense means lived or dwelt in a place.

clue.text: Call again on Minister to come to the question

blocks.note: Rev is short for Reverend, the title of a minister of religion
'is it?' is a question in its own right

explanation.surface: A minister being urged to get to the point of an awkward matter.
explanation.definitionFit: To revisit someone is to pay them a further visit, going back to see them once more.

clue.text: With waves all round, say, leaves Auntie's organisation

definitions.text: With waves all round, say, leaves

indicators.note: organising a set of things means arranging them into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written, the S included

explanation.surface: Someone departs the BBC (nicknamed Auntie) as trouble swirls around the corporation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auntie' is a fond British nickname for the BBC, so 'leaves Auntie's organisation' reads as quitting the broadcaster; in fact 'leaves' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanists call a leaf sinuate when its margin is wavy, curving in and out all the way around.

clue.text: GP not fit for practice

blocks.note: a GP (general practitioner) is a doctor, abbreviated Dr
someone not fit is unwell

explanation.surface: A family doctor judged unfit to keep running a medical practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Practice' looks like a doctor's surgery; here it means repeated training.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill is a routine exercise repeated for training, like a fire drill or army parade practice.

clue.text: Pet name taken from wild flower

blocks.note: a dog is a typical household pet
Violet is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An animal's name borrowed from a flower growing in the hedgerow.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog violet is a common scentless species of violet growing wild in woods and hedges.

clue.text: Accountant cautions partnership

blocks.note: CA stands for chartered accountant
hoots of a horn are warnings

explanation.surface: An accountant warns a client about the terms of a business partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in cahoots is to be in secret league with someone, a collusive alliance.

clue.text: Attractive girl that's following fashion

indicators.note: coming after something means the second piece is placed behind the first

blocks.note: the cut of a garment is its style or fashion
i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A pretty young woman who keeps up with every trend.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutie is informal for a cute, appealing person, usually a pretty young woman.

clue.text: Revamped chain stores bottom of trade league

indicators.note: something revamped has been remade, so its letters come out in a new order
to store something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange
a seat is the bottom one sits on

explanation.surface: A retail chain's makeover leaves it at the foot of a commercial league table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chain stores' reads as shops, but stores is a verb here: the rearranged chain holds the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hanseatic League was the medieval alliance of north German trading towns, so the adjective describes that commercial union.

clue.text: Writer so close to the bone - gets it again about right?

indicators.note: getting something again and turning it about suggests reworking the letters into a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An author whose work cuts so near the knuckle that critics slam him once more.
explanation.walkthrough: John Osborne wrote Look Back in Anger, famous for writing close to the bone, so the surface fits him.
explanation.definitionFit: John Osborne was the English playwright behind Look Back in Anger, the original Angry Young Man.

clue.text: It may be worn when a wester's got up

indicators.note: something got up is dressed or contrived, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, the possessive S included

explanation.surface: Something you'd put on when a westerly gale has risen.
explanation.walkthrough: A wester is a westerly wind; 'got up' sounds like the wind rising.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweater is a knitted jumper, a garment pulled on over the top half of the body.

clue.text: What Kiev has to offer literally is marketing

blocks.note: the final letter of the city's name

blocks.clueFragment: What Kiev has to offer literally
blocks.note: taken literally, the word Kiev has a V as its ending

explanation.surface: Asking what Ukraine's capital has to sell to the world.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, Kiev has a V ending: V + ENDING.
explanation.definitionFit: Vending is selling goods, so it can stand for marketing them to customers.

clue.text: You mean two jurors are incompetent? That's with defence potential

blocks.note: if two of a twelve-person jury are out, ten remain
the rest of the jury are competent, i.e. able

explanation.surface: A lawyer's indignant question in court about a jury, leading to talk of the defence.
explanation.walkthrough: A jury has twelve members; if two are incompetent, ten are able: TEN ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenable position is one that can be held or defended against attack or argument.

clue.text: Of little moment? Moment indeed!

blocks.note: first meaning: unimportant, minor league
second meaning: read literally, a moment is a small span of time

explanation.walkthrough: 'Moment' means importance in the first half and a brief instant in the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Small-time describes something minor or insignificant, while a moment is literally only a short stretch of the clock.

clue.text: Show contrition, having run off with leggy bird

indicators.note: something that has run off has left, so the letter for run is dropped

blocks.note: to regret is to show remorse
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone apologising after fleeing with a long-legged wading bird.
explanation.walkthrough: REGRET loses its first R to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a type of heron, a wading bird with long slender legs.

clue.text: Small numbers from Dublin? They fit the brogue!

indicators.note: spoken in a Dublin accent, the TH comes out as a plain T

blocks.note: threes are small numbers; in a Dublin accent the TH becomes a T

explanation.surface: An Irish joke: a brogue is both an Irish accent and a sturdy shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: A brogue is a stout leather shoe as well as an Irish accent; the accent gives the sound, the shoe gives the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoe trees are shaped inserts pushed inside shoes to keep them in shape when not worn.

clue.text: Good smart pithy quote

blocks.note: sound means good, reliable
to smart is to sting, as a bite does

explanation.surface: Praise for a clever, concise quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: A soundbite is a short punchy extract from a speech, quoted in news reports.

clue.text: Projectile's journey long - no beginning or end but a great distance

indicators.note: without a beginning the first word loses its opening letter, and without an end the second loses its last

blocks.note: a missile's path through the air is its flight
to long for something is to yearn

explanation.surface: A missile's trip that goes on and on, seemingly without start or finish.
explanation.walkthrough: FLIGHT loses its F and YEARN its N.
explanation.definitionFit: A light year is the distance light travels in a year, a huge astronomical measure of length.

clue.text: Dressed overall, wearing ensign, about to cast off

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the first pair is read backwards

blocks.note: dressed in clothes means wearing them
rag is slang for a flag
to shed is to cast off

explanation.surface: A ship decked in flags from stem to stern, flying its ensign, about to sail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressed overall' is a naval term for a ship decorated with flags; cast off sounds like the ship leaving its moorings.
explanation.definitionFit: Garnished means adorned or decorated, as a ship dressed overall is adorned with a full set of flags.

clue.text: Vainglorious competitor uses drug - horse?

blocks.note: pot is slang for cannabis
a hunter is a horse bred for hunting

explanation.surface: A boastful rider suspected of doping, or perhaps of doping his horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot-hunter enters contests chiefly to win trophies (pots), a prize-grabbing competitor.

clue.text: Troops look to retreat under umbrella

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word is read in the other direction
in a down entry, one piece written under another follows it

blocks.note: paras are paratroopers
lo is an old word meaning look!

explanation.surface: Soldiers seek cover beneath an umbrella-like canopy as they fall back.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol is a light umbrella carried to give shade from the sun.

clue.text: Tuft of grass turned over, giving cover to bird

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so the word is read backwards
in a down entry, a covering piece sits on top, so it comes first

blocks.note: grass and pot are both slang for cannabis
the knot is a wading bird

explanation.surface: A clump of grass is flipped over to provide shelter for a nesting bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A topknot is a tuft of hair or feathers on the top of the head.

clue.text: Not an entire fowl?

blocks.note: surface reading: a bird that is only partly there, say a portion of chicken
setter's reading: an entire animal is an uncastrated male, so this is a castrated cockerel

explanation.walkthrough: In animal husbandry 'entire' means not castrated, so a fowl that is not entire is a neutered cock.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a cockerel castrated to fatten it for the table.

clue.text: Peak shortly after taking professional qualification

indicators.note: cut short, a word loses its final letter
one piece comes after the other, so the second follows the first

blocks.note: pro is short for professional
the peak of a cap is its visor

explanation.surface: Someone reaches the summit of a career soon after earning a professional certificate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Professional qualification' reads as a diploma, but qualification is the definition and professional gives PRO; VISOR loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a condition or stipulation attached to an agreement, so it qualifies the terms.

clue.text: Flat refusal to go on working - and it's multilateral

blocks.note: a flat refusal is a plain no
to go on at someone is to nag them
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A union's outright refusal to keep working, agreed on all sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Multilateral' sounds like diplomacy; literally it means many-sided.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonagon is a polygon with nine sides, so literally a many-sided figure.

clue.text: Shoot as Gunners drop back

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the word is read right to left

blocks.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners of the British Army
a dip is a drop

explanation.surface: Artillerymen fire as they fall back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gunners' is also the nickname of Arsenal football club, but here it means the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapid is a fast stretch of river, and a shoot is likewise a stretch of swift water or chute.

clue.text: Press on with the descent, say

indicators.note: say signals that the words are to be spoken rather than read

blocks.note: the descent is the route downwards

explanation.surface: Urging someone to keep going on the way down a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press on' looks like 'keep going'; here it means press down upon.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh down is to press heavily upon something, burdening it with weight.

clue.text: Spa town

blocks.note: first meaning: a spa is a mineral spring, a source of water like a well
second meaning: a small cathedral city in Somerset, England

explanation.walkthrough: Wells in Somerset is England's smallest city, named for its springs.
explanation.definitionFit: Wells are springs of water, as at a spa, and Wells is a cathedral city in Somerset.

clue.text: Fantastic Hera, foremost of Olympian goddesses

indicators.note: something fantastic is fanciful or bizarre, so its letters are put into a strange new order
the foremost part of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Hera, queen of the gods, hailed as the greatest of the Olympian goddesses.
explanation.definitionFit: The Horae were the Greek goddesses of the seasons and natural order, attendants of the Olympians.

clue.text: Supplier of The Times daily? Wrong, almost daily!

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the letters get rearranged
almost all of a word means its last letter is dropped

blocks.note: the Sun is a British daily newspaper
taken as written, the letters to shorten and rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a supplier delivers The Times newspaper every day, then corrects themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Times' looks like the newspaper, so a newsagent; the Sun, another paper, gives the first part, and a sundial tells the time every day.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundial shows the time of day from the sun's shadow, so it supplies the times.

clue.text: What's a pitcher doing in this game?

blocks.note: first meaning: a pitcher at baseball is throwing the ball hard
second meaning: the Irish field sport played with sticks and a ball

explanation.walkthrough: The baseball pitcher makes you think of America; the game is Irish hurling, played with a stick called a hurley.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurling means throwing forcefully, and hurling is also the fast Irish stick-and-ball field sport.

clue.text: Learning notes

blocks.note: first meaning: scholarship
second meaning: written messages sent by post

explanation.definitionFit: Letters means literature and scholarship, and letters are also short written messages or correspondence.

clue.text: Soften colour, say, by adding blue

indicators.note: say tells us to go by how the word is spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: to dye is to colour
feeling blue is feeling down

explanation.surface: Instructions for toning down a shade by mixing in some blue.
explanation.definitionFit: When noise or wind dies down it becomes quieter and gentler, so it softens or subsides.
